speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether the Ministry or Animal and Veterinary Service (AVS) works with Animal Welfare Groups (AWGs) on the operations of the Trap-Neuter-Rehome/Release-Manage programme; and (b) if so, whether consultations take place between the AWGs and AVS before every trapping operation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In situations that present risk to public safety, AVS will intervene swiftly.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: AVS will continue to work closely with TNRM partners in the management of free-roaming dogs to safeguard both public safety and well-being of the dogs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: AVS colleagues and I visited our partners last week to discuss ways we can better collaborate moving forward.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For instance, we intend to review joint protocols and further improve communication and coordination.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These build on existing collaboration channels, such as TNRM rehoming efforts, outreach and AVS-led adoption drives.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are almost at the end of Question Time, so keep your supplementary question short.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: First, what is the nature of such discussions with the different Animal Welfare Groups (AWGs) prior to, perhaps, trapping operations?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Behind every animal held is a human and an AWG where they celebrate every rescue, recovery and adoption and feeling the grief when an animal suffers.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: The work is built on care, and it has not been easy.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: At the same time, I have also personally interacted with so many dedicated AVS and National Parks Board (NParks) officers, so I wanted to do a special thanks for their commitment for this constant work with the AWGs to rehome animals and balance the competing needs with care and professionalism.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: The second question really is then: can the Minister of State provide an assessment on the effectiveness of the TNRM programme so far?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I am heartened to know that a review is due.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: So, what will this review entail and how will it be done?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I hope and I urge AVS and NParks to continue working closely with the AWGs to further improve the TNRM methods.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: That also includes streamlining feedback channels and conducting regular stakeholder engagements and workshops.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I am very happy that many of our partners will be joining this TNRM workshop for us to continue to refine these processes.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we will continue to continue to work with our TNRM partners to further refine these processes for the well-being of our dogs.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Clarification by Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs.

speaker: Mr Speaker
